dimensions.assessment: Affects state, local, tribal, campus, and territorial law enforcement personnel, as well as communities and individuals targeted by transnational repression.
dimensions.evidence: enhance the capabilities of State, local, Tribal, campus, and territorial law enforcement personnel... to counter transnational repression

dimensions.assessment: Improves protective capabilities, training, and resources for vulnerable communities and law enforcement agencies.
dimensions.evidence: provide personal safety best practices for individuals and communities that may be targets or are victims of transnational repression

dimensions.assessment: The source does not specify appropriations or new federal spending amounts.
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish formal training requirements, community briefings, and research coordination.
dimensions.evidence: Subtitle H of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 361 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent training mandates accompanied by a Comptroller General review report due within two years.
dimensions.evidence: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report on the implementation... not later than two years after the date of the enactment

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary allocations required to execute the training program are not stated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates the Department of Homeland Security to develop specialized training programs and community awareness briefings for state, local, and tribal law enforcement to combat transnational repression.
